steps.text: Every property of metals and non-metals is used in real life. Let's match materials to the right job.
For each use, pick the material whose property fits — copper wires (conducts electricity), iron girders (strong), a bell (sonorous metal), a pencil lead of graphite (non-metal).
Choosing a material means matching its property to the need. That's why we pick metals for wires, tools and bells, and non-metals where those properties would be wrong.

coach.mission: Match each real-world use to the right material.
whenStuck: Tap “Start”, then think about which property each job needs.
Ask: does this use need conducting, bending, ringing, or none of those?
whenWrong: Match the property to the need — wires need a conductor, so a metal.
If the job needs a poor conductor or something brittle, that's a non-metal.
whenCorrect: Right — that material's property is exactly what the job needs.
Good — you matched the property to the real-world use.
coach.done: You've connected metal and non-metal properties to everyday uses. Explore more, or move on when you're ready.
